title: cost-opt: autotune batching/caching defaults, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Marcus Ortega
release_notes: Introduces an autotuner for batching and caching defaults, quantization profile suggestions, and initial unit-economics tooling (CLI + dashboard). No breaking API changes. Feature gated behind `autotune.cost_opt` flag.
description:
Motivation: many customers are running inference with suboptimal batching/caching defaults and conservative quantization settings. This PR implements an autotuner that profiles production traffic and recommends conservative defaults for batching, caching TTLs, and quantization profiles to reduce per-token costs while maintaining latency SLOs. It also adds a lightweight unit-economics (uecon) tooling suite (CLI + dashboard integration) to surface estimated $/1k tokens and expected savings for suggested changes.

What changed (high level): - runtime/autotune: new autotuner service that samples request size/latency distributions, runs offline MCMC-style parameter search against policies (batch size limits, max wait, cache TTL) and scores candidates by a cost + SLA penalty objective. - runtime/kernels: plumbing to accept autotuner-suggested defaults at startup; can be overridden per-deployment. - model-profiles/quant: added quantization-profile recommendations module; profiles include fp16, int8, and hybrid presets with estimated perf/cost tradeoffs. - uecon: CLI `redwood-uecon estimate` and a server endpoint to feed the Console dashboard with simulated savings. - tests: integration tests for autotuner against a synthetic traffic generator, unit tests for scoring function, e2e smoke for CLI. - docs: added a new how-to and best-practices doc for enabling autotune and interpreting recommendations.

Checklist: - [x] autotuner algorithm + scoring implemented - [x] feature toggles and config schema added - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] docs and Console wiring - [x] rollout plan and kill-switch in code - [x] performance benchmarks (internal)

Notes: - Autotune runs by default in dry-run mode; customer-visible changes require explicit approval in Console or enabling `autotune.apply=true` in deployment config. - Quant profiles are advisory by default; applying quant requires model artifact compatibility checks (handled by model-registry integration).

Related: ENG-4821 tracks UX for review/approval flows, ENG-4899 tracks follow-ups for Dedicated autoscale interaction.
